chunks: “If you come to the well while you are in janabah, and you do not find a bucket nor anything with which to draw [water], then perform tayammum with the earth, for indeed the Lord of the water and the Lord of the earth are One. And do not fall into the well, and do not spoil the people’s water for them.”
Then al-Shaykh, may Allah Ta'ala support him, said: Even if it is abundant, he has acted contrary to the sunnah (prophetic tradition) by performing ghusl in it. That is indicated by the following.

— (427) 118 — What al-Shaykh, may Allah Ta'ala support him, informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', who said:

I wrote to the one who was asked about a pond in which rainwater gathers, or into which water is drawn from a well, and in which a person cleans himself after urine, or in which the junub performs ghusl: what is its limit beyond which it is not permissible? So he wrote: “Do not perform wudu (ablution) from the like of this except in a case of necessity requiring it.”

His statement, عليه السلام, “Do not perform wudu (ablution) from the like of this except in a case of necessity requiring it,” indicates the reprehensibility of entering it, because had it not been disliked, he would not have restricted performing wudu (ablution) and ghusl from it to the state of necessity. As for what indicates that the water is not spoiled when it exceeds a kurr by the junub entering it, it is what has previously come in the reports: that when water reaches a kurr, nothing renders it impure.

key_terms.الصَّعِيدِ: earth or ground used for tayammum
key_terms.الْبِئْرَ: the well serving as a shared water source
key_terms.الْغَدِيرِ: a pond or pool where water gathers
key_terms.الْكُرِّ: the legal measure of abundant water not easily affected by impurity
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.ضَرُورَةٍ: a state of necessity that permits otherwise restricted use
key_terms.فَتَيَمَّمْ: perform tayammum as a substitute purification when water cannot properly be used
key_terms.لَا يُنَجِّسُهُ شَيْءٌ: nothing renders it impure when the legal condition is met

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a junub entering a well or using pond water for purification in Shi'i fiqh?
ai.summary: This passage addresses rulings related to janabah, tayammum, and the use of standing water for purification. It indicates that one should avoid entering or contaminating shared water sources, while also clarifying that water exceeding the measure of kurr is not rendered impure merely by the junub entering it, though doing so may be contrary to the sunnah (prophetic tradition) or disliked.
